record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: For a set of reals X, let O be the family of open covers of X, Ω the family of open ω-covers (every finite subset of X is contained in some member), and Γ the family of open γ-covers (infinite covers in which each point belongs to all but finitely many members). The property Sfin(A,B) means that from each cover in a sequence from A one can choose finitely many members so that the union of all chosen members is a cover in B; Ufin(A,B) is the analogous finite-selection property for sequences of covers with no finite subcover, where the sequence of finite unions belongs to B. Suppose X is a subset of a Borel set B ⊆ R and X satisfies Ufin(O, Γ). Must there exist a σ-compact set F with X ⊂ F ⊂ B? Is the answer still yes when B is an Fσδ set?

evidence.quote: Assume that X ⊆ B ⊆ R, B is Borel, and X satisfies Ufin(O, Γ). Must there be a σ-compact F with X ⊂ F ⊂ B? What if B is Fσδ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a separable metric space, viewed as a subspace of the real line R. For a collection A of open covers of X, let O denote all open covers, Ω the open ω-covers (those open covers U such that every finite subset of X is contained in some single member of U), and Γ the open γ-covers (infinite open covers U such that every point of X lies in all but finitely many members of U).

For two such collections A and B, the selection principle Ufin(A, B) asserts that whenever (U_n : n ∈ N) is a sequence of members of A such that no U_n contains a finite subcover of X, there exist finite subfamilies F_n ⊆ U_n with the property that the cover { ⋃ F_n : n ∈ N } belongs to B.

A subset F of R is σ-compact if it is a countable union of compact sets. A subset B of R is Fσδ if it is a countable intersection of Fσ sets.

Question. Suppose X ⊆ B ⊆ R, where B is a Borel set and X has the property Ufin(O, Γ) (i.e. X is a Hurewicz space). Must there exist a σ-compact set F with X ⊆ F ⊆ B? Does the answer remain affirmative under the stronger hypothesis that B is an Fσδ set?
artifact.status_search_result: Banakh and Zdomskyy (Topology Appl. 156 (2008), 10–15) showed that the Gδ-separation property is equivalent to the Hurewicz property, but consistently (e.g. under the set-theoretic hypothesis b = d) there is a Hurewicz subspace of a Borel/Fσδ ambient space that is not contained in any σ-compact subset of that ambient space. Hence the answer to both questions is consistently "no", giving a negative consistency answer; a definitive ZFC resolution is not visible in the search results, so the problem appears to be at least partially resolved (negatively, modulo consistency assumptions).

status_evidence.title: Separation properties between the σ-compactness and Hurewicz property (Banakh–Zdomskyy)
status_evidence.snippet: Under b=d there exists a Borel space X and a Hurewicz subspace H of X such that X is the union of a Polish space and a σ-compact space, but no σ-compact subspace of X contains H; the Gδ- and Fσδ-separation properties are distinct.
status_evidence.claim: It is consistent that a Hurewicz subset of a Borel (indeed Fσδ-like) ambient space cannot be enclosed in any σ-compact intermediate set, so the σ-compact interpolation question has a consistent negative answer.

status_evidence.title: Hurewicz spaces are sigma-compact-like (Dan Ma's Topology Blog)
status_evidence.snippet: A metrizable space X is Hurewicz iff for any embedding into a Polish space there is a σ-compact set A with X ⊂ A. For Gδ-sets G ⊃ X there is an Fσ set F with X ⊂ F ⊂ G.
status_evidence.claim: The Gδ case of the σ-compact interpolation problem is known to hold, characterizing the Hurewicz property.
